Hands-on activity · printable card

Quick card · AI for screening and extraction

View source on GitHubLast updated 3 November 2026

Question: Are hand hygiene interventions effective in reducing healthcare-associated infections? Compare with: the reference review, Pruna et al., J Clin Med 2026 (12 included studies; screening and extraction by two human reviewers without AI; provisional). Do not open it before step 3. Full guide: activity/README.md (on your own: section "Doing it on your own (self-paced)", 60-90 min)

Roles
Driver types and runs the tool
Prompter writes prompts, pastes the criteria verbatim
Verifier checks every quote and number in the source
Recorder AI use record + discrepancy log

Include only if ALL are met
C1 Acute care hospital (not long-term care, outpatient, rehabilitation, veterinary)
C2 Hospital-wide or more than one ward (not a single ICU, NICU, ED or unit)
C3 Multimodal hand hygiene intervention, clearly central (not one isolated measure; not a broad bundle)
C4 Interrupted time series or before-after (not RCTs, cross-sectional, outbreak reports, reviews)
C5 At least one clinical HAI outcome (not only compliance or hand rub use)
C6 English

Step 1 · Screening · 10 min Chat: batch 1 (R001-R020) from the records page. Agent: all 60. Output record_id,decision,reason · decision include | exclude | unsure · reason = criterion. Count the rows back; verifier checks 3 decisions against the abstract. In doubt or no abstract: unsure. Save screening_run1.csv. Spare minute: same prompt in a new chat, save screening_run2.csv.

Step 2 · Extraction · 12 min Read the form first (data/extraction_form.csv, 11 core fields). One paper per chat (chat: Phan2020.txt, study_id Phan2020). Output study_id,field,value,source_quote,location. Verbatim quote for every value; not reported is allowed. Verifier: Ctrl+F three quotes. Save extraction.csv.

Step 3 · Compare · 8 min (now open answers/) Browser scorer, or: python3 activity/tools/score_screening.py screening_run1.csv --compare screening_run2.csv (agent: add --expect-all) python3 activity/tools/score_extraction.py extraction.csv Read the coverage line first ("Screened 20 of 60" is expected in the chat track), then: missed includes · QUOTE NOT FOUND · unsupported · false absent. Log 3 discrepancies in worksheets/discrepancy_log.md: who is right, after checking the source.

Ask yourselves: Performance: would we accept this sensitivity? Transparency: can we trace every value? Bias: whose errors, which studies? Oversight: who signs the table? Reproducibility: did two runs agree? And the reference: is it always right?

For learning only. These prompts are teaching material for this workshop. They are not a validated method. If you are not confident with how large language models work (context windows, parsing, sampling, retrieval, hallucination) and with advanced techniques (structured outputs, verification against the source, reproducibility checks, documentation of model and version), do not use AI to conduct a real evidence review. You stay responsible for every decision: the AI does not.
